text: Vietnam's packaging sector needs stronger support to meet global standards

Speaking at a November 2026 trade promotion briefing organized by the Vietnam Trade Promotion Agency (VIETRADE) under the Ministry of Industry and Trade in Ho Chi Minh City, Ms. Le Thi Nhu Hanh, Standing Vice President of the Vietnam Packaging Association (Vinpas), reported that packaging exports across four key product groups reached approximately $1.47 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up nearly 11 percent year on year.

Among these four pillars, flexible plastic packaging led with nearly $1 billion (up 15 percent), followed by labels at $269 million (up over 3 percent), paperboard boxes at $108 million (down 7 percent), and corrugated cartons at nearly $99 million (up over 10 percent).
However, total exports equaled only about 62 percent of the sector's $2.38 billion import bill during the same period.
Despite reaching demanding markets such as the US, Japan, Germany, the Netherlands, and Australia, Vietnam ' s market share remains tiny.
In 2025, Vietnam supplied just 0.3 percent of France ' s $36 million corrugated carton imports and 0.8 percent of the UK ' s $47.6 million imports.
Within ASEAN, Vietnam accounted for roughly 2 percent of Indonesi a' s $149.8 million paperboard box imports and under 0.5 percent of Singapore ' s $56.8 million corrugated carton imports.
Mr. Le Hoang Tai, Deputy Director General of VIETRADE, noted that exporters face tightening technical, safety, traceability, and environmental standards alongside tariff shifts and price competition.
VINPAS identified three core obstacles holding back local firms.

First, import regulations are growing stricter, exemplified by the EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) effective August 12, US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) rules, and strict food-contact controls in Japan and Australia.

Second, international retailers increasingly demand specialized certifications such as BRCGS Packaging Materials, Forest Stewardship Council (FSC), and Global Recycled Standard (GRS), alongside rigorous testing for barrier properties, compression strength, and chemical migration.

Third, many manufacturers lack accredited test results and technical dossiers to prove compliance; for instance, a local food exporter had to import jar lids because domestic suppliers lacked BPA-free gasket certification.

Because export efforts remain largely fragmented, Vinpas proposed that VIETRADE and Vietnam ' s overseas trade offices strengthen support in three areas: providing targeted market and regulatory intelligence, facilitating trade matching and international fair participation such as the Vietnam International Paper and Packaging Exhibition (VPPE), and establishing a regular coordination mechanism to collect buyer feedback and upgrade industry standards.
